summary: This document deprecates the RSASHA1 and RSASHA1-NSEC3-SHA1 algorithms for creating DNSKEY and RRSIG records. It updates RFC 4034 and RFC 5155.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9905 deprecates RSASHA1 and RSASHA1-NSEC3-SHA1 for creating DNSSEC records because SHA-1 is no longer advisable and support is not fully interoperable. Validators must still support checking these algorithms, but must treat their records as insecure.

questions: which dnssec algorithms does rfc 9905 deprecate
can resolvers still validate sha-1 dnssec signatures
what should dns operators do about rsasha1
subtitle: Deprecating two SHA-1-based algorithms for DNSSEC signing

tldr.problem: SHA-1's cryptographic strength has diminished, and its use in DNSSEC signatures is no longer advisable.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC says RSASHA1 and RSASHA1-NSEC3-SHA1 MUST NOT be used to create DS, DNSKEY or RRSIG records, while validators MUST continue to support validation with them.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9905 updates RFC 4034 and RFC 5155 and tells operators to switch to stronger algorithms listed in the IANA registries.

facts.label: Use for DNSKEY and RRSIG creation

today: RFC 9905 updates RFC 4034 and RFC 5155 to deprecate two SHA-1-based DNSSEC algorithms.

sections.title: Why DNSSEC Deprecates SHA-1
sections.content:
The RFC says the security protection provided by SHA-1 has diminished as attacks have weakened its cryptographic basis. DNSSEC used SHA-1 in RRSIG and DS records, but stronger alternatives are available and some systems have removed support for validating SHA-1-based signatures.

As a result, SHA-1 is no longer fully interoperable for DNSSEC and its use is no longer advisable. The RFC deprecates RSASHA1 and RSASHA1-NSEC3-SHA1.
sections.plainLanguage: SHA-1-based DNSSEC signatures have become less reliable and are not supported everywhere. The RFC therefore deprecates two algorithms that use SHA-1.

sections.title: Signing and Validation Rules
sections.content:
RSASHA1 and RSASHA1-NSEC3-SHA1 MUST NOT be used to create DS records or DNSKEY and RRSIG records. Validating resolvers MUST treat DS records using these algorithms as insecure; if no DS record with an accepted algorithm is available, records below the delegation point MUST be treated as insecure.

Validating resolver implementations MUST continue to support validation using the algorithms. They must treat SHA-1 signing algorithms as unsupported for establishing security, and responses are insecure if no other supported signature can validate them.
sections.plainLanguage: Do not create new DNSSEC records with these SHA-1 algorithms. Validators still need to recognize them, but must not treat their signatures as secure.

sections.title: Operator Transition
sections.content:
Zone owners using SHA-1-based algorithms should immediately switch to stronger algorithms, such as those recommended in the IANA DNSKEY and DS registries.

The RFC notes that some software packages and operating systems may already have removed SHA-1 support. Operators may need to build and deploy software manually to continue supporting the specified validation requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: Zone owners should move to stronger algorithms listed in the IANA registries. Operators may need to check software support during the change.
